A.explanation: About $1.5\text{ V}$ cannot be obtained when the $9.6\text{ V}$, $8.4\text{ V}$ and $6.3\text{ V}$ emfs and the three $IR$ drops around loop PQR are all included.

B.explanation: $2.1\text{ V}$ is $8.4 - 6.3$ in volts and ignores the $9.6\text{ V}$ battery and the potential drop across the resistor between P and Q.

C.explanation: The resistor drop is $2.5\text{ V}$ and acting against the $9.6\text{ V}$ battery between P and Q gives $|9.6 - 2.5| = 7.1\text{ V}$.

D.explanation: $12.1\text{ V}$ is $9.6 + 2.5$ in volts and adds the resistor drop instead of subtracting it for the P to Q path.

hints: Notice PQR is a single loop with three emfs $9.6\text{ V}$, $8.4\text{ V}$ and $6.3\text{ V}$ in series with three identical resistors of resistance $R$.
Use Kirchhoff second law around PQR: two batteries drive current one way round the loop and the $8.4\text{ V}$ battery drives the opposite way, so the net emf is $9.6 + 6.3 - 8.4$.
First find the common current and hence the $IR$ drop across each identical resistor, then step from P to Q through the $9.6\text{ V}$ battery and one resistor.
walkthrough: Treat PQR as one series loop. Let each identical resistor be $R$ and let internal resistance be zero, so total resistance is $3R$.

Apply Kirchhoff second law round the loop. With the polarities shown, the $9.6\text{ V}$ and $6.3\text{ V}$ batteries act together against the $8.4\text{ V}$ battery, so net emf $E_{net} = 9.6 + 6.3 - 8.4 = 7.5\text{ V}$.
The loop current is $I = E_{net} / 3R = 7.5 / (3R)$. Hence the magnitude of the potential drop across each identical resistor is $V_R = IR = 7.5 / 3 = 2.5\text{ V}$.

Step from P to Q along the top branch containing the $9.6\text{ V}$ battery and one resistor. Going from the battery positive toward negative, potential falls by $9.6\text{ V}$, but the resistor drop of $2.5\text{ V}$ acts in the opposite sense for this path.
The magnitude is therefore $|V_P - V_Q| = |9.6 - 2.5| = 7.1\text{ V}$. This is option C.
